COMPUTER STUDIES MARCH — TERMLY EXAM #5
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: COMPUTER STUDIES MARCH
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. Internal Cooking Timer
   B. Information and Communication Technology
   C. Input Cable Tester
   D. International Cricket Team

2. When learning Professional Ethics and Legal Issues in Computing, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Professional Ethics and Legal Issues in Computing.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Professional Ethics and Legal Issues in Computing.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Professional Ethics and Legal Issues in Computing.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Professional Ethics and Legal Issues in Computing.

3. When learning Data Analysis and Visualisation, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Data Analysis and Visualisation.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Data Analysis and Visualisation.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Data Analysis and Visualisation.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Data Analysis and Visualisation.

4. When learning Career Opportunities, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Career Opportunities.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Career Opportunities.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Career Opportunities.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Career Opportunities.

5. When learning Emerging Technologies, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Emerging Technologies.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Emerging Technologies.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Emerging Technologies.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Emerging Technologies.

6. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Work alone with eyes closed
   B. Wear safety gear and follow instructions
   C. Remove all guards
   D. Run with the tool

7. When learning Cybersecurity, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Cybersecurity.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Cybersecurity.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Cybersecurity.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Cybersecurity.

8. When learning Data Structures, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Data Structures.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Data Structures.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Data Structures.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Data Structures.

9. When learning Social and Ethical Issues in Networking, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Social and Ethical Issues in Networking.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Social and Ethical Issues in Networking.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Social and Ethical Issues in Networking.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Social and Ethical Issues in Networking.

10. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Overload every socket
   B. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun
   C. Ignore burnt cables
   D. Never touch live wires with wet hands

11. When learning Robotics, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Robotics.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Robotics.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Robotics.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Robotics.

12. When learning Artificial Intelligence Concepts, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Artificial Intelligence Concepts.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Artificial Intelligence Concepts.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Artificial Intelligence Concepts.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Artificial Intelligence Concepts.

13. When learning Artificial Intelligence Implications and Ethics, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Artificial Intelligence Implications and Ethics.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Artificial Intelligence Implications and Ethics.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Artificial Intelligence Implications and Ethics.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Artificial Intelligence Implications and Ethics.

14. When learning Cloud Computing, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Cloud Computing.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Cloud Computing.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Cloud Computing.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Cloud Computing.

15. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. CPU
   B. Keyboard
   C. Speaker
   D. Monitor

16. When learning Network Troubleshooting, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Network Troubleshooting.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Network Troubleshooting.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Network Troubleshooting.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Network Troubleshooting.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Emerging Technologies and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Artificial Intelligence Concepts and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Artificial Intelligence Implications and Ethics and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Robotics and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Data Analysis and Visualisation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Career Opportunities and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
